title.zh: 卷九十七 志第五十 河渠七
title.raw: 卷九十七 志第五十 河渠七 Volume 97 Treatises 50: Rivers and Canals 7

sentences.zh: 淮郡諸水

translations.literal: Waters of the Huai Prefecture Region
translations.idiomatic: Waters of the Huai Prefecture Region

sentences.zh: 淮郡諸水：紹興初，以金兵蹂踐淮南，猶未退師，四年，詔燒毀揚州灣頭港口閘、泰州薑堰、通州白莆堰，其餘諸堰，並令守臣開決焚毀，務要不通敵船；

translations.literal: Waters of the Huai Prefecture Region: In the early Shaoxing era, because Jin troops had ravaged the region south of the Huai and had not yet withdrawn, in the fourth year an edict ordered the burning and destruction of the sluice at Yangzhou Wandou Harbor, the Jiang Weir at Taizhou, and the Baipu Weir at Tongzhou; all other weirs as well were to be breached and burned by frontier officials, so that enemy vessels could by no means pass;
translations.idiomatic: Waters of the Huai Prefecture Region: Early in the Shaoxing era, with Jin armies still ravaging the Huai south country and not yet withdrawn, in the fourth year the court ordered the sluice at Yangzhou's Wandou Harbor, the Jiang Weir at Taizhou, and the Baipu Weir at Tongzhou burned and destroyed; every other weir was likewise to be opened, breached, and burned by local officials, so enemy ships could not pass at all;

sentences.zh: 又詔宣撫司毀拆真、揚堰閘及真州陳公塘，無令走入運河，以資敵用。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered the Pacification Commission to demolish the weirs and sluices of Zhen and Yang and the Chen Gong Pond at Zhenzhou, lest they drain into the Grand Canal to supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered the Pacification Commission to tear down the weirs and sluices at Zhen and Yang and the Chen Gong Pond at Zhenzhou, so their waters would not flow into the Grand Canal for the enemy's use.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，詔淮南宣撫司，募民開浚瓜洲至淮口運河淺澀之處。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, an edict directed the Huainan Pacification Commission to recruit civilians to dredge the shallow, silted sections of the canal from Guazhou to the Huai mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, the Huainan Pacification Commission was ordered to recruit laborers to dredge the shallow, choked reaches of the canal from Guazhou to the Huai estuary.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，以和州守臣言，開鑿姥下河，東接大江，防捍敵人，檢制盜賊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao, on the recommendation of the Hezhou prefect, the Laoxia River was cut open, joining the great river to the east to ward off enemies and control bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiandao, acting on the Hezhou prefect's memorial, the Laoxia River was excavated to link with the Yangtze on the east, to block enemies and restrain bandits.

sentences.zh: 六年，淮東提舉徐子寅言：「淮東鹽課，全仰河流通快。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Huaidong Intendant Xu Ziyin said: "The salt levy of eastern Huai depends entirely on swift river transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Xu Ziyin, intendant of eastern Huai, reported: "Eastern Huai's salt revenue depends wholly on a fast, open river.

sentences.zh: 近運河淺澀，自揚州灣頭港口至鎮西山光寺前橋垛頭，計四百八十五丈，乞發五千餘卒開浚。

translations.literal: Recently the canal has grown shallow and silted. From Yangzhou Wandou Harbor to the bridge head before Xiguang Temple at Zhenxi, a total of 485 zhang — I request dispatch of more than five thousand troops to dredge it.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the canal has shoaled and silted up. From Yangzhou's Wandou Harbor to the bridge head before Xiguang Temple at Zhenxi — 485 zhang in all — I ask that more than five thousand soldiers be sent to dredge it.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，詔令淮南漕臣，自洪澤至龜山淺澀之處，如法開撩。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, an edict ordered Huainan transport officials to dredge shallow places from Hongze to Guishan according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year, Huainan transport commissioners were ordered to dredge every shallow stretch from Hongze to Guishan by the same method.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年四月，詔築泰州月堰，以遏潮水。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Chunxi, an edict ordered construction of the Moon Weir at Taizhou to check the tide.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Chunxi, the court ordered the Moon Weir built at Taizhou to hold back the tide.

sentences.zh: 從守臣張子正請也。

translations.literal: This followed a request from the prefect Zhang Zizheng.
translations.idiomatic: This granted the request of Prefect Zhang Zizheng.

sentences.zh: 八年，提舉淮南東路常平茶鹽趙伯昌言：「通州、楚州沿海，舊有捍海堰，東距大海，北接鹽城，袤一百四十二里。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zhao Bochang, intendant for Ever-Normal Granaries and Tea-Salt on the Eastern Route of Huainan, said: "Along the coast of Tongzhou and Chuzhou there was formerly a sea-defence weir, reaching the great sea on the east and connecting with Yancheng on the north, 142 li in length.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Zhao Bochang, intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries and Tea-Salt for eastern Huainan, memorialized: "Along the Tongzhou and Chuzhou coast stood an old sea-defence weir, 142 li from the eastern sea to Yancheng in the north.

sentences.zh: 始自唐黜陟使李承實所建，遮護民田，遮罩鹽灶，其功甚大。

translations.literal: It was first built by the Tang imperial inspector Li Chengshi; it sheltered the people's fields and shielded the salt pans — its merit was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Tang inspector Li Chengshi first built it to shelter farmland and shield the salt pans — a work of great benefit.

sentences.zh: 歷時既久，頹圮不存。

translations.literal: With the passage of time it had long since crumbled and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years it had collapsed until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 至本朝天聖改元，范仲淹為泰州西溪鹽官日，風潮泛溢，渰沒田產，毀壞亭灶，有請於朝，調四萬餘夫修築，三旬畢工。

translations.literal: In our dynasty at the inauguration of the Tiansheng era, when Fan Zhongyan served as salt commissioner at Xixi in Taizhou, wind and tide flooded outward, inundating fields and destroying sheds and pans. Petitions reached the court; more than forty thousand laborers were mobilized to rebuild; the work was finished in thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, at the opening of the Tiansheng era, when Fan Zhongyan was salt commissioner at Xixi in Taizhou, surging wind and tide drowned the fields and wrecked sheds and pans. The court was petitioned; more than forty thousand workers were mobilized to rebuild the weir, and the work was finished in thirty days.

sentences.zh: 遂使海瀕沮洳瀉鹵之地，化為良田，民得奠居，至今賴之。

translations.literal: Thus the damp, brackish land along the sea became good fields; the people could settle securely and still rely on it today.
translations.idiomatic: Brackish marsh along the shore became fertile farmland; the people could live in peace, and the region still depends on it today.

sentences.zh: 自後浸失修治，才遇風潮怒盛，即有沖決之患。

translations.literal: Afterwards maintenance was gradually neglected; whenever wind and tide surged violently, breaches followed.
translations.idiomatic: Maintenance was then allowed to lapse; whenever wind and tide ran high, the weir was breached.

sentences.zh: 自宣和、紹興以來，屢被其害。

translations.literal: From the Xuanhe and Shaoxing eras onward, the harm recurred repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xuanhe and Shaoxing reigns onward, disaster struck again and again.

sentences.zh: 阡陌洗蕩，廬舍漂流，人畜喪亡，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Fields were washed away, dwellings swept off, men and livestock lost beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were scoured bare, houses swept away, and men and livestock lost beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 每一修築，必請朝廷大興工役，然後可辦。

translations.literal: Each time rebuilding was needed, the court had to be asked for major works before it could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Every repair required a petition to the throne for a massive public works campaign before anything could be done.

sentences.zh: 望令淮東常平茶鹽司：今後捍海堰如有塌損，隨時修葺，務要堅固，可以經久。

translations.literal: I hope the Eastern Huai Ever-Normal Granaries and Tea-Salt office may be ordered: hereafter whenever the sea-defence weir suffers collapse or damage, repair it at once and make it solid so it may endure.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Eastern Huai Ever-Normal Granaries and Tea-Salt office be instructed: whenever the sea-defence weir collapses or is damaged, repair it promptly and keep it strong enough to last.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 九年，淮南漕臣錢沖之言：「真州之東二十里，有陳公塘，乃漢陳登浚源為塘，用救旱饑。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Huainan transport official Qian Chongzhi said: "Twenty li east of Zhenzhou is Chen Gong Pond, which in Han times Chen Deng dug at its source to form a pond for relieving drought and famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Qian Chongzhi, Huainan transport commissioner, reported: "Twenty li east of Zhenzhou lies Chen Gong Pond. In Han times Chen Deng excavated its source to form a reservoir against drought and famine.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符間，江、淮制置發運置司真州，歲藉此塘灌注長河，流通漕運。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era the Jiang-Huai transport command established its dispatch office at Zhenzhou; yearly it drew on this pond to feed the long river and keep grain transport flowing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era the Jiang-Huai transport office was set at Zhenzhou; each year it drew on this pond to feed the main channel and keep the grain fleet moving.

sentences.zh: 其塘周回百里，東、西、北三面，倚山為岸，其南帶東，則系前人築壘成堤，以受啟閉。

translations.literal: The pond runs a hundred li in circuit. East, west, and north lean on mountains as banks; on the south and east predecessors built ramparts into an embankment for opening and closing the gates.
translations.idiomatic: The pond measures a hundred li around. On the east, west, and north its banks rest against the hills; to the south and east earlier builders raised ramparts into an embankment to control opening and closing.

sentences.zh: 廢壞歲久，見有古來基趾，可以修築，為旱乾溉田之備。

translations.literal: Ruined for many years, ancient foundations remain and may be rebuilt as a reserve for irrigation in drought.
translations.idiomatic: Long ruined, its ancient footings can still be rebuilt as a reserve to irrigate fields in dry years.

sentences.zh: 凡諸場鹽綱、糧食漕運、使命往還，舟艦皆仰之以通濟，其利甚博。

translations.literal: Salt convoys, grain transport, and mission traffic all depend on it for passage — the benefit is very broad.
translations.idiomatic: Salt fleets, grain barges, and official missions all rely on it for passage — the benefit is immense.

sentences.zh: 本司自發卒貼築周回塘岸，建置斗門、石鹈達各一所，乞於揚子縣尉階銜內帶'兼主管陳公塘'六字，或有損壞，隨時補築，庶幾久遠，責有所歸。」

translations.literal: This office has dispatched troops to reinforce the pond banks all around and established one sluice gate and one stone pelican sluice each. I ask that the Yangzi county magistrate's rank-title include the six characters "concurrently supervise Chen Gong Pond," so that any damage may be repaired at once and responsibility may endure."
translations.idiomatic: This office has sent troops to shore up the pond banks and built one sluice gate and one stone pelican sluice. I ask that the Yangzi county magistrate's title include "concurrently supervising Chen Gong Pond," so damage is repaired promptly and accountability endures."

sentences.zh: 十二年，和州守臣請於千秋澗置斗門，以防麻澧湖水泄入大江，遇歲旱灌溉田疇，實為民利。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Hezhou prefect asked to place a sluice gate at Qianqiu Stream to keep Mali Lake water from draining into the great river, and in drought years to irrigate fields — a real benefit to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Hezhou prefect asked for a sluice gate at Qianqiu Stream to keep Mali Lake from emptying into the Yangtze and, in dry years, to irrigate the fields — a clear benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 十四年，揚州守臣熊飛言：「揚州運河，惟藉瓜洲、真州兩閘瀦積。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Yangzhou prefect Xiong Fei said: "The Yangzhou canal relies solely on impoundment at the two sluices of Guazhou and Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Xiong Fei, prefect of Yangzhou, reported: "The Yangzhou canal depends entirely on impoundment at the Guazhou and Zhenzhou sluices.

sentences.zh: 今河水走泄，緣瓜洲上、中二閘久不修治，獨潮閘一坐，轉運、提鹽及本州共行修整，然迫近江潮，水勢沖激，易致損壞；

translations.literal: Now the water runs off because the upper and middle sluices at Guazhou have long gone unrepaired; only the Tide Sluice remains, which transport, the salt intendant, and this prefecture jointly maintain — yet it lies close to river tide and the current strikes hard, so damage comes easily;
translations.idiomatic: Water is now leaking away because Guazhou's upper and middle sluices have long gone unrepaired; only the Tide Sluice remains, which transport, the salt intendant, and this prefecture maintain together — yet it sits against the river tide, where the current strikes hard and damage comes easily;

sentences.zh: 真州二閘，亦復損漏。

translations.literal: the two sluices at Zhenzhou have likewise leaked and failed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhou's two sluices have also broken and leak.

sentences.zh: 令有司葺理上、下二閘，以防走泄。

translations.literal: I ask that the responsible offices repair the upper and lower sluices to prevent loss of water.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the authorities repair the upper and lower sluices to stop the leakage.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年，淮東提舉陳損之言：「高郵、楚州之間，陂湖渺漫，茭葑彌滿，宜創立堤堰，以為瀦泄，庶幾水不至於泛溢，旱不至於乾涸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxi, Huaidong Intendant Chen Sunzhi said: "Between Gaoyou and Chuzhou lakes and marshes stretch wide, smartweed and rush choke them full. Embankments and weirs should be newly built for storage and release, so that in flood the water may not overflow and in drought it may not run dry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxi, Chen Sunzhi, Huaidong intendant, memorialized: "Between Gaoyou and Chuzhou, lakes and marshes spread wide and reeds and smartweed choke them. New embankments and weirs should be built for storage and release, so floods do not spill over and drought does not parch the land.

sentences.zh: 乞興築自揚州江都縣至楚州淮陰縣三百六十里，又自高郵、興化至鹽城縣二百四十里，其堤岸傍開一新河，以通舟船。

translations.literal: I ask to raise works from Jiangdu County, Yangzhou, to Huaiyin County, Chuzhou — 360 li — and from Gaoyou and Xinghua to Yancheng County — 240 li — with a new canal opened beside the embankment for vessels.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to build 360 li from Jiangdu in Yangzhou to Huaiyin in Chuzhou, and another 240 li from Gaoyou and Xinghua to Yancheng, cutting a new canal along the embankment for boats.

sentences.zh: 仍存舊堤以捍風浪，載柳十余萬株，數年後堤岸亦牢，其木亦可備修補之用。

translations.literal: Keep the old embankment to withstand wind and waves; plant more than a hundred thousand willows — in a few years the embankment will be firm and the timber may serve for repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the old embankment to break wind and waves, and plant more than a hundred thousand willows; in a few years the embankment will stand firm and the timber can supply repairs.

sentences.zh: 兼揚州柴墟鎮，舊有堤閘，乃泰州泄水之處，其閘壞久，亦于此創立斗門。

translations.literal: At Chaiyu Town in Yangzhou there was formerly an embankment sluice, the place where Taizhou discharges water; the sluice has long been ruined — here too establish a sluice gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou's Chaiyu Town stood an old embankment sluice where Taizhou drains its water; long ruined, it too should receive a new sluice gate.

sentences.zh: 西引盱眙、天長以來眾湖之水，起自揚州江都，經由高郵及楚州寶應、山陽，北至淮陰，西達於淮；

translations.literal: Draw the waters of the many lakes from Xuyi and Tianchang westward, beginning at Jiangdu in Yangzhou, passing Gaoyou and Baoying and Shanyang in Chuzhou, north to Huaiyin, and west to the Huai;
translations.idiomatic: Channel the lakes west of Xuyi and Tianchang from Yangzhou's Jiangdu through Gaoyou and Chuzhou's Baoying and Shanyang to Huaiyin in the north and the Huai in the west;

sentences.zh: 又自高郵入興化，東至鹽城而極於海；

translations.literal: also from Gaoyou into Xinghua, east to Yancheng and on to the sea;
translations.idiomatic: also from Gaoyou into Xinghua, east to Yancheng and the sea;

sentences.zh: 又泰州海陵南至揚州泰興而徹于江：共為石鹈達十三，斗門七。

translations.literal: and from Hailing in Taizhou south to Taixing in Yangzhou and out to the river: thirteen stone pelican sluices and seven sluice gates in all.
translations.idiomatic: and from Taizhou's Hailing south to Yangzhou's Taixing and the river — thirteen stone pelican sluices and seven sluice gates in all.

sentences.zh: 乞以紹熙堰為名，鑱諸堅石。

translations.literal: I ask that it be named the Shaoxi Weir and cut into solid stone."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the work be named the Shaoxi Weir and inscribed on solid stone."

sentences.zh: 」淮田多沮洳，因損之築堤捍之，得良田數百萬頃。

translations.literal: Huai fields are mostly damp and marshy; because of Chen Sunzhi's building embankments to hold them back, millions of qing of good land were gained.
translations.idiomatic: Huai farmland was largely boggy marsh; by building embankments to hold the water back, Chen Sunzhi reclaimed millions of qing of good land.

sentences.zh: 奏聞，除直秘閣、淮東轉運判官。

translations.literal: When the memorial was reported, he was appointed Direct Gentleman of the Secretariat and Huaidong transport vice-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, he was made Direct Gentleman of the Secretariat and vice-commissioner of Huaidong transport.

sentences.zh: 浙江通大海，日受兩潮。

translations.literal: The Zhe River reaches the great sea and daily receives both tides.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe River opens to the ocean and twice a day receives the tide.

sentences.zh: 梁開平中，錢武肅王始築捍海塘，在候潮門外。

translations.literal: In the Kaiping era of Liang, King Qian the Martial and Solemn first built a sea-defence embankment outside the Tide-Watching Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's Kaiping era, King Qian the Martial and Solemn first built a sea-defence embankment outside the Tide-Watching Gate.

sentences.zh: 潮水晝夜沖激，版築不就，因命強弩數百以射潮頭，又致禱胥山祠。

translations.literal: Day and night the tide struck; plank-and-earth work would not hold, so he ordered several hundred strong crossbows to shoot at the tide head and also offered prayer at the Mount Xu shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night the tide hammered the works; rammed-earth construction would not stand, so he set several hundred powerful crossbows to shoot at the tide crest and prayed at the Mount Xu shrine.

sentences.zh: 既而潮避錢塘，東擊西陵，遂造竹器，積巨石，植以大木。

translations.literal: Then the tide turned aside from Qiantang and struck Xiling to the east; they fashioned bamboo frames, piled great stones, and planted large timbers.
translations.idiomatic: The tide then turned aside from Qiantang and struck Xiling to the east; they made bamboo cages, piled great stones, and drove in heavy timbers.

sentences.zh: 堤岸既固，民居乃奠。

translations.literal: Once the embankment was firm, the people's dwellings were secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the embankment held firm, the people could settle in safety.

sentences.zh: 逮宋大中祥符五年，杭州言浙江擊西北岸益壞，稍逼州城，居民危之。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu in Song, Hangzhou reported that the Zhe River was battering the northwest bank ever more severely and pressing toward the prefectural city, putting the people in peril.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu in Song, Hangzhou reported that the Zhe River was eating the northwest bank and edging toward the city, putting residents at risk.

sentences.zh: 即遣使者同知杭州戚綸、轉運使陳堯佐畫防捍之策。

translations.literal: The court at once dispatched envoys together with Hangzhou vice-prefect Qi Lun and transport commissioner Chen Yaozuo to devise defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The court immediately sent envoys with Vice-Prefect Qi Lun of Hangzhou and Transport Commissioner Chen Yaozuo to plan defenses.

sentences.zh: 綸等因率兵力，籍梢楗以護其沖。

translations.literal: Lun and the others then led military labor and deployed piles and fenders to shield the impact.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Lun and his colleagues then mobilized troops and set piles and fenders to break the surge.

sentences.zh: 七年，綸等既罷去，發運使李溥、內供奉官盧守懃經度，以為非便。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, after Lun and the others had left office, dispatch commissioner Li Pu and palace attendant Lu Shouqin surveyed the works and judged them unsatisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after Qi Lun and his colleagues had left office, Dispatch Commissioner Li Pu and Palace Attendant Lu Shouqin inspected the works and found them inadequate.

sentences.zh: 請復用錢氏舊法，實石於竹籠，倚疊為岸，固以樁木，環亙可七里。

translations.literal: They asked to restore the old method of the Qian clan: pack stones in bamboo cages, layer them as a bank, secure them with piles, and ring the shore for nearly seven li.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to restore the Qian family's old method: stones packed in bamboo cages, stacked into a bank, pinned with piles, running nearly seven li along the shore.

sentences.zh: 斬材役工，凡數百萬，逾年乃成；

translations.literal: Timber was cut and labor mobilized, several million in all; after more than a year the work was finished;
translations.idiomatic: Timber was felled and workers mobilized by the millions; after more than a year the work was finished;

sentences.zh: 而鉤末壁立，以捍潮勢，雖湍湧數丈，不能為害。

translations.literal: the hooked ends stood vertical to repel the tide; though the surge rose several zhang, it could do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: the hooked faces stood vertical to break the tide; even when the surge rose several zhang, it could not harm the bank.

sentences.zh: 至景祐中，以浙江石塘積久不治，人患墊溺，工部郎中張夏出使，因置捍江兵士五指揮，專採石修塘，隨損隨治，眾賴以安。

translations.literal: By the Jingyou era the stone embankment along the Zhe River had long gone unmaintained; people feared drowning in collapse. Langzhong of the Ministry of Works Zhang Xia went on mission and established five commands of river-defense troops dedicated to quarrying stone and repairing the embankment, mending damage as it occurred; the multitude relied on this for safety.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jingyou era the Zhe River stone embankment had long gone unrepaired, and people feared being drowned when it failed. Zhang Xia of the Ministry of Works, sent on inspection, created five river-defense commands to quarry stone and repair the embankment as damage appeared; the people lived in safety because of it.

sentences.zh: 邦人為之立祠，朝廷嘉其功，封甯江侯。

translations.literal: The people raised a shrine to him; the court praised his merit and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pacifying the River.
translations.idiomatic: The people built him a shrine; the court honored his service and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pacifying the River.

sentences.zh: 及高宗紹興末，以錢塘石岸毀裂，潮水漂漲，民不安居，令轉運司同臨安府修築。

translations.literal: By the end of Shaoxing under Gaozong, the Qiantang stone bank had cracked and the tide flooded in; the people could not live in peace. The transport office and Lin'an prefecture were ordered to rebuild.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Gaozong's Shaoxing reign, the Qiantang stone bank shattered and the tide surged inland, unsettling the people. The transport office and Lin'an prefecture were ordered to rebuild.

sentences.zh: 孝宗乾道九年，錢塘廟子灣一帶石岸，復毀於怒潮。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao under Xiaozong, the stone bank at Miaozi Bay along the Qiantang was again destroyed by raging tide.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Qiandao under Emperor Xiaozong, the stone bank at Qiantang's Miaozi Bay was again wrecked by furious tide.

sentences.zh: 詔令臨安府築填江岸，增砌石塘，淳熙改元，復令有司：「自今江岸沖損，以乾道修治為法。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lin'an prefecture to fill the river bank and add stone embankment work. At the change to Chunxi, officials were again ordered: "From now on, wherever the river bank is damaged, follow the Qiandao repairs as the standard."
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Lin'an to fill the river bank and add stone embankment work. At the opening of Chunxi, officials were told again: "Hereafter, wherever the river bank is damaged, use the Qiandao repairs as the model."

sentences.zh: 理宗寶祐二年十二月，監察御史兼崇政殿說書陳大方言：「江潮侵齧堤岸，乞戒飭殿、步兩司帥臣，同天府守臣措置修築，留心任責，或有潰決，咎有攸歸。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Baoyou under Lizong, Supervising Censor and Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall Chen Dafang said: "The river tide is eating the embankment. I ask that the commanders of the Hall and Step Armies and the capital prefect be warned to arrange repairs together, attend to their duty, and bear blame if there is a breach."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Baoyou, Supervising Censor and Lecturer Chen Dafang at the Chongzheng Hall said: "The tide is gnawing the embankment. I ask that the commanders of the Hall and Step Armies and the capital prefect be instructed to repair together, take responsibility seriously, and be held accountable if the bank fails."

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，監察御史兼崇政殿說書李衢言：「國家駐蹕錢塘，今逾十紀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, Supervising Censor and Lecturer Li Qu said: "The state has made its seat at Qiantang for more than ten reigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year, Supervising Censor and Lecturer Li Qu said: "The dynasty has dwelt at Qiantang for more than ten reigns.

sentences.zh: 惟是浙江東接海門，胥濤澎湃，稍越故道，則沖齧堤岸，蕩析民居，前後不知其幾。

translations.literal: Only the Zhe River east joins the sea gate; the Xu tide surges; if it slightly overruns its old course, it gnaws the embankment and scatters dwellings — how many times before and after, none can say.
translations.idiomatic: Only east of the Zhe River lies the sea gate; the Xu tide runs fierce. If it strays even slightly from its old channel, it eats the embankment and scatters houses — countless times before and since.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，造捍江五指揮，兵士每指揮以四百人為額。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era the five river-defense commands were created; each command was fixed at four hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingli era five river-defense commands were created, each fixed at four hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 今所管才三百人，乞下臨安府拘收，不許占破。

translations.literal: Those now on the rolls number only three hundred. I ask Lin'an prefecture to muster them and forbid diversion.
translations.idiomatic: Today they number only three hundred. I ask Lin'an to muster the full quota and forbid their being diverted.

sentences.zh: 及從本府收買樁石，沿江置場樁管，不得移易他用。

translations.literal: Also have this prefecture purchase piles and stone, set up storage yards along the river, and forbid their use elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Let the prefecture also buy piles and stone, set riverside storage yards, and forbid their use elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 仍選武臣一人習于修江者，隨其資格，或以副將，或以路分鈐轄系銜，專一鈐束修江軍兵，值有摧損，隨即修補；

translations.literal: Further select one military officer skilled in river repair and, according to rank, attach him as deputy commander or circuit controller to oversee the river-defense troops exclusively; whenever damage occurs, repair at once;
translations.idiomatic: Select one military officer skilled in river works and, according to rank, give him a deputy or circuit-controller title to command the river troops exclusively; whenever damage appears, repair it at once;

sentences.zh: 或不勝任，以致江潮沖損堤岸，即與責罰。」

translations.literal: if he is not equal to the task and the tide damages the embankment, let him be punished."
translations.idiomatic: if he proves unfit and the tide breaches the embankment, punish him."

sentences.zh: 臨安西湖周回三十里，源出於武林泉。

translations.literal: The West Lake of Lin'an measures thirty li in circuit; its source is the Wulin spring.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an's West Lake measures thirty li around; it rises from Wulin Spring.

sentences.zh: 錢氏有國，始置撩湖兵士千人，專一開浚。

translations.literal: When the Qian clan held the state, a corps of a thousand lake-dredging soldiers was first established for exclusive dredging.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qian house ruled, they first raised a thousand lake-dredging troops devoted solely to clearing the lake.

sentences.zh: 至宋以來，稍廢不治，水涸草生，漸成葑田。

translations.literal: Since Song times it has been gradually neglected; the water dried up, grass grew, and it slowly became rush fields.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song times maintenance has lapsed; the water shrank, grass took hold, and the lake slowly turned to rush fields.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，知杭州蘇軾奏謂：「杭之為州，本江海故地，水泉咸苦，居民零落。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era, Su Shi as prefect of Hangzhou memorialized: "Hang as a prefecture was originally coastal marshland; its springs were brackish and bitter, and the people were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era, Su Shi as prefect of Hangzhou wrote: "Hangzhou was originally coastal marsh; its water was brackish and bitter and the people few.

sentences.zh: 自唐李泌始引湖水作六井，然後民足于水，井邑日富，百萬生聚，待此而食。

translations.literal: From Tang times Li Bi first drew lake water to make six wells; then the people had enough water, towns grew daily, and a million souls gathered, depending on this for their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, Li Bi first drew lake water into six wells; then the people had water enough, the city prospered, and a million souls lived here, fed by the lake.

sentences.zh: 今湖狹水淺，六井盡壞，若二十年後，盡為葑田，則舉城之人，復飲咸水，其勢必耗散。

translations.literal: Now the lake is narrow and shallow and the six wells are all ruined. In twenty years it will all be rush fields; then everyone in the city will again drink brackish water, and the population will surely disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Now the lake is narrow and shallow and all six wells are ruined. In twenty years it will be rush fields again; then the whole city will drink brackish water and the people will surely scatter.

sentences.zh: 又放水溉田，瀕湖千頃，可無凶歲。

translations.literal: Releasing water also irrigates fields; a thousand qing along the lake can be free of famine years.
translations.idiomatic: Releasing lake water also irrigates fields; a thousand qing along the shore can escape famine.

sentences.zh: 今雖不及千頃，而下湖數十里間，茭菱谷米，所獲不貲。

translations.literal: Though it no longer reaches a thousand qing, for several tens of li below the lake the water chestnuts, rice, and grain harvested are beyond price.
translations.idiomatic: Though it no longer reaches a thousand qing, for tens of li below the lake the water chestnuts, rice, and grain harvested are beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 又西湖深闊，則運河可以取足於湖水，若湖水不足，則必取足于江潮。

translations.literal: Also, if the West Lake is deep and broad, the canal can draw fully on lake water; if the lake is insufficient, it must draw fully on the river tide.
translations.idiomatic: If West Lake is deep and wide, the canal can draw fully from the lake; if the lake runs low, the canal must draw from the tidal river instead.

sentences.zh: 潮之所過，泥沙渾濁，一石五鬥，不出三載，輒調兵夫十余萬開浚。

translations.literal: Where the tide passes, the silt is muddy; five dou of mud in every stone — within three years more than a hundred thousand troops must be mobilized for dredging.
translations.idiomatic: Where tide water passes, silt is thick — five parts mud in ten of water — and within three years more than a hundred thousand laborers must be sent to dredge again.

sentences.zh: 又天下酒官之盛，如杭歲課二十余萬緡，而水泉之用，仰給於湖。

translations.literal: Also, of all the empire's wine monopolies, Hang's yearly levy exceeds two hundred thousand strings of cash, and its water supply depends on the lake.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the empire's wine monopolies, Hangzhou's yearly levy exceeds two hundred thousand strings, and its water depends on the lake.

sentences.zh: 若湖漸淺狹，少不應溝，則當勞人遠取山泉，歲不下二十萬工。

translations.literal: If the lake grows ever shallower and narrow and cannot answer the ditches, then labor must be spent fetching mountain spring water — no less than two hundred thousand workdays a year.
translations.idiomatic: If the lake keeps shrinking and cannot feed the channels, laborers must haul mountain spring water — no less than two hundred thousand workdays a year.

sentences.zh: 」因請降度牒減價出賣，募民開治。

translations.literal: He therefore asked to issue reduced-price ordination certificates and recruit the people to clear the lake.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked to sell ordination certificates at reduced price and recruit civilians to dredge the lake.

sentences.zh: 禁自今不得請射、侵佔、種植及臠葑為界。

translations.literal: From now on petition grants, encroachment, planting, and staking rush boundaries are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that petition grants, encroachment, planting, and rush-fence boundaries be forbidden from that time on.

sentences.zh: 以新舊菱蕩課利錢送錢塘縣收掌，謂之開湖司公使庫，以備逐年雇人開葑撩淺。

translations.literal: The profit from old and new water-chestnut and rush leases was sent to Qiantang County to hold in the Open-Lake Office public treasury, to hire men each year to cut rush and dredge shallows.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue from old and new water-chestnut and rush leases was paid to Qiantang County's Open-Lake Office treasury to hire men yearly to cut rush and dredge shallows.

sentences.zh: 縣尉以「管勾開湖司公事」系銜。

translations.literal: The county magistrate bore the added title "supervising Open-Lake Office affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate took the added title "supervising Open-Lake Office affairs."

sentences.zh: 軾既開湖，因積葑草為堤，相去數里，橫跨南、北兩山，夾道植柳，林希榜曰「蘇公堤」，行人便之，因為軾立祠堤上。

translations.literal: After Su opened the lake, he piled dredged rush into an embankment several li apart, spanning the southern and northern hills, planted willows along the road, and Lin Xi inscribed it "Su Embankment." Travelers found it convenient, and a shrine to Su was raised on the embankment.
translations.idiomatic: After Su dredged the lake, he piled the dredged rush into an embankment miles apart, spanning the southern and northern hills, with willows planted along the path. Lin Xi inscribed it "Su Embankment." Travelers were spared a long detour, and a shrine to Su was built on the embankment.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，以張澄奏請，命臨安府招置廂軍兵士二百人，委錢塘縣尉兼領其事，專一浚湖；

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, on Zhang Cheng's memorial, Lin'an prefecture was ordered to recruit two hundred garrison soldiers, entrusted to the Qiantang county magistrate for exclusive lake dredging;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, on Zhang Cheng's memorial, Lin'an was ordered to recruit two hundred garrison soldiers, placed under the Qiantang county magistrate to dredge the lake exclusively;

sentences.zh: 若包占種田，沃以糞土，重寘於法。

translations.literal: if anyone encroached to plant fields or enriched soil on the lake bed, punish severely by law.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who encroached to farm or dumped soil on the lake bed was to be punished severely.

sentences.zh: 十九年，守臣湯鵬舉奏請重開。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the prefect Tang Pengju memorialized asking for a major reopening.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Prefect Tang Pengju asked for a full reopening.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，守臣周淙言：「西湖水面唯務深闊，不容填溢，並引入城內諸井，一城汲用，尤在涓潔。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao, Prefect Zhou Cong said: "The West Lake surface must be kept deep and broad, not allowed to be filled in; it also feeds all wells within the city — the whole city's water supply depends on its clarity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiandao, Prefect Zhou Cong said: "West Lake must be kept deep and wide, never filled in. It also feeds every well in the city — the whole capital depends on its clarity.

sentences.zh: 舊招軍士止有三十餘人，今宜增置撩湖軍兵，以百人為額，專一開撩。

translations.literal: Formerly only a little more than thirty soldiers were recruited; now the lake-dredging garrison should be increased to a quota of a hundred for exclusive dredging.
translations.idiomatic: Only a little more than thirty soldiers were recruited before; now the lake-dredging garrison should be raised to a hundred for exclusive dredging.

sentences.zh: 或有種植茭菱，因而包占，增疊堤岸，坐以違制。」

translations.literal: If anyone plants water chestnuts or rush and thereby encroaches, piling up the embankment, punish as a violation of statute."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who plants rush or water chestnuts, encroaches, and builds up the embankment should be punished for violating statute."

sentences.zh: 九年，臨安守臣言：「西湖冒佃侵多，葑茭蔓延，西南一帶，已成平陸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Lin'an prefect reported: "Encroachment on West Lake has grown; rush and reeds have spread, and the southwestern stretch has become dry land.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the Lin'an prefect reported: "Encroachment on West Lake has grown; reeds have spread until the southwestern shore is dry land.

sentences.zh: 而瀕湖之民，每以葑草圍裹，種植荷花，駸駸不已。

translations.literal: Yet lakeside people keep fencing with rush, planting lotus, and pressing ever onward.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lakeside residents keep fencing with rush, planting lotus, and pressing ever farther out.

sentences.zh: 恐數十年後，西湖遂淤，將如越之鑒湖，不可復矣。

translations.literal: I fear that in several decades West Lake will silt up, like Yue's Mirror Lake, beyond recovery.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in a few decades West Lake will silt solid, like Mirror Lake in Yue, never to be restored.

sentences.zh: 乞一切芟除，務令淨盡，禁約居民，不得再有圍裹。

translations.literal: I ask that everything be cut away and cleared completely, and residents forbidden to fence again.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all encroachments be cut away and cleared, and residents forbidden to fence the lake again.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 臨安運河在城中者，日納潮水，沙泥渾濁，一汛一淤，比屋之民，委棄草壤，因循填塞。

translations.literal: The canal within Lin'an city daily admits tidal water; the silt is muddy, and each tide silts it anew. Householders dump soil and grass, and by custom the channel fills in.
translations.idiomatic: The canal inside Lin'an admits the tide each day; silt is thick, and every tide chokes it anew. Households dump soil and refuse, and by habit the channel fills.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，守臣蘇軾奏謂：「熙寧中，通判杭州時，父老皆云苦運河淤塞，率三五年常一開浚。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era Prefect Su Shi memorialized: "In the Xining era, when I was vice-prefect of Hangzhou, the elders all said the canal silted painfully and had to be dredged every three to five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanyou era Prefect Su Shi wrote: "In the Xining era, when I was vice-prefect of Hangzhou, elders said the canal silted badly and had to be dredged every three to five years.

sentences.zh: 不獨勞役兵民，而運河自州前至北郭，穿闤闠中蓋十四五里，每將興工，市肆洶動，公私騷然。

translations.literal: Not only did it weary soldiers and civilians, but from before the prefecture to North Gate the canal runs fourteen or fifteen li through the market — whenever work began, shops were thrown into uproar and public and private affairs were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: It wearied troops and people alike, and from the prefectural seat to North Gate the canal runs fourteen or fifteen li through the markets — whenever dredging began, shops were thrown into uproar and public and private life was disrupted.

sentences.zh: 自胥吏、壕砦兵級等，皆能恐喝人戶，或云當於某處置土、某處過泥水，則居者皆有失業之憂。

translations.literal: From clerks, moat-garrison soldiers, and the like, all could intimidate households, saying soil must be placed at such-and-such a spot or muddy water run through such-and-such a place — then those who lived there all had fears of losing their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks, moat-garrison soldiers, and the like could bully householders, saying soil had to be dumped here or muddy water run through there — and everyone along the route feared losing their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 既得重賂，又轉而之他。

translations.literal: Once they had received heavy bribes, they moved on to others.
translations.idiomatic: After taking heavy bribes, they moved on to extort someone else.

sentences.zh: 及工役既畢，則房廊、邸舍，作踐狼籍，園圃隙地，例成丘阜，積雨蕩濯，復入河中，居民患厭，未易悉數。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, verandas and lodges were trampled into disorder; vacant garden plots routinely became mounds; accumulated rain washed the spoil back into the river — the people's distresses are not easily counted.
translations.idiomatic: When the work ended, verandas and lodges lay trampled and ruined; vacant plots became heaps of spoil; rain washed it all back into the canal — the harm to residents is beyond easy reckoning.

sentences.zh: 若三五年失開，則公私壅滯，以尺寸水行數百斛舟，人牛力盡，跬步千里，雖監司使命，有數日不能出郭者。

translations.literal: If for three or five years dredging was neglected, both public and private traffic stagnated; a few inches of water carried a boat of hundreds of hu; men and oxen exhausted themselves — a thousand li in every short step; even supervisory commissioners on mission might several days fail to leave the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: If dredging was skipped for three to five years, traffic stalled public and private alike — a few inches of water for a boat of hundreds of hu, men and oxen spent for every yard, and even commissioners on royal business could be trapped outside the wall for days.

sentences.zh: 詢其所以頻開屢塞之由，皆云龍山浙江兩閘，泥沙渾濁，積日稍久，便及四五尺，其勢當然，不足怪也。

translations.literal: Asking why it was opened often yet silted repeatedly, all said at the two sluices at Long Hill and the Zhe River the mud was muddy; after days it reached four or five chi — such was the nature, nothing to marvel at.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why dredging bought so little time, everyone said the Long Hill and Zhe River sluices sent muddy silt that in a few days piled four or five chi deep — to be expected, they said, not worth marveling at.

sentences.zh: 尋剗刷捍江兵士及諸色廂軍，得一千人，七月之間，開浚茅山、鹽橋二河，各十餘里，皆有水八尺。

translations.literal: Soon mustered Jiang-defense soldiers and various garrison troops, obtaining a thousand men; within the seventh month dredged the Mao Hill and Salt Bridge rivers, each more than ten li, all with eight chi of water.
translations.idiomatic: He then mustered Jiang-defense troops and various garrison soldiers, a thousand in all; within a seventh-month season he dredged the Mao Hill and Salt Bridge rivers, more than ten li each, to a depth of eight chi throughout.

sentences.zh: 自是公私舟船通利，三十年以來，開河未有若此深快者。

translations.literal: From then on public and private boats passed smoothly; in thirty years of canal-opening there had been none so deep and satisfying.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private shipping ran freely after that — in thirty years of dredging, none had been so thorough.

sentences.zh: 然潮水日至，淤塞猶昔，則三五年間，前功復棄。

translations.literal: Yet the tide came daily and silting was as before; in three or five years the former work would again be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tide came daily and silt returned as before, so within three or five years the work would be undone again.

sentences.zh: 今于鈐轄司前置一閘，每遇潮上，則暫閉此閘，候潮平水清復開，則河過闤闠中者，永無潮水淤塞、開淘騷擾之患。

translations.literal: Now before the Military Commission office place one sluice; whenever the tide rises, temporarily close it; when the tide is flat and the water clear, open again — then the canal passing through the market will forever lack the troubles of tidal silting and dredging disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a sluice be built before the Military Commission: close it when the tide rises, open it when the water clears — then the market stretch of canal would forever be free of tidal silt and the uproar of repeated dredging.

sentences.zh: 」詔從其請，民甚便之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his request; the people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved, to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年十一月，宰臣奏開修運河淺澀，帝曰：「可發旁郡廂軍、壯城、捍江之兵，至於廩給之費，則不當吝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Shaoxing, chief ministers memorialized dredging the shallow Grand Canal. The Emperor said: "Send garrison, stronghold, and Jiang-defense troops from neighboring prefectures; as for grain payments, do not be stinting."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Shaoxing, the chief ministers proposed dredging the shallow canal. The Emperor said: "Send garrison, stronghold, and river-defense troops from neighboring prefectures — and do not stint on provisions."

sentences.zh: 」宰臣朱勝非等曰：「開河非今急務，而饋餉艱難，為害甚大。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Zhu Shengfei and others said: "Opening the canal is not today's urgent task, yet supply transport is difficult — the harm is very great."
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Zhu Shengfei and others replied: "Dredging is not the most urgent matter now, yet grain transport is already strained — the harm would be great."

sentences.zh: 時方盛寒，役者良苦，臨流居人，侵塞河道者，悉當遷避；

translations.literal: The season was bitter cold; laborers would suffer greatly; those living by the stream who encroached and blocked the channel must all be relocated;
translations.idiomatic: It is deep winter — the laborers would suffer; every riverside dweller who has encroached on the channel must be moved;

sentences.zh: 至於畚閘所經，沙泥所積，當預空其處，則居人及富家以僦屋取貲者皆非便，恐議者以為言。

translations.literal: As to where baskets and sluices pass and silt piles, those places must be cleared in advance — then residents and rich families who rented houses for profit would all be inconvenienced; we fear critics will complain.
translations.idiomatic: Where dredgers and sluice works must pass, spoil must be piled — those spots must be cleared beforehand, inconveniencing residents and landlords who rent for income; critics will surely object.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「禹卑宮室而盡力於溝洫，浮言何恤焉！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Yu built mean palaces and devoted his strength to ditches — why heed idle words!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Yu kept his palace humble and poured his strength into the waterways — why heed idle talk!"

sentences.zh: 」八年，又命守臣張澄發廂軍、壯城兵千人，開浚運河堙塞，以通往來舟楫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, again ordered the prefect Zhang Cheng to mobilize a thousand garrison and stronghold troops to dredge the blocked canal for passing boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he again ordered Prefect Zhang Cheng to raise a thousand garrison and stronghold troops to clear the canal for shipping.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年，守臣吳芾言：「城裏運河，先已措置北梅家橋、仁和倉、斜橋三所作壩，取西湖六處水口通流灌入。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longxing, Prefect Wu Bi said: "Within the city canal, dams were already set at North Meijia Bridge, Renhe Granary, and Xie Bridge, drawing from six West Lake outlets."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longxing, Prefect Wu Bi reported: "Along the city canal we have already dammed North Meijia Bridge, Renhe Granary, and Xie Bridge, drawing water from six West Lake outlets."

sentences.zh: 府河積水，至望仙橋以南至都亭驛一帶，河道地勢，自昔高峻。

translations.literal: The prefectural river pooled water; from south of Wangxian Bridge to Duting Post the channel's ground had always been high and steep.
translations.idiomatic: Water pools in the prefectural canal; from south of Wangxian Bridge to Duting Post the bed has always been high and steep.

sentences.zh: 今欲先於望仙橋城外保安閘兩頭作壩，卻于竹車門河南開掘水道，車戽運水，引入保安門通流入城，遂自望仙橋以南開至都亭驛橋，可以通徹積水，以備緩急。

translations.literal: Now we wish first to dam both ends of the outer Bao'an Sluice at Wangxian Bridge, then dig a channel south of Zhuche Gate, scoop water by wheel, lead it through Bao'an Gate into the city, and open from south of Wangxian Bridge to Duting Post Bridge to drain pooled water for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: We propose first to dam the outer Bao'an Sluice at Wangxian Bridge, then dig a channel south of Zhuche Gate and scoop water through Bao'an Gate into the city, opening from Wangxian Bridge south to Duting Post Bridge to drain standing water for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 計用工四萬。

translations.literal: Estimated labor: forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Estimated labor: forty thousand work-units.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 乾道三年六月，知荊南府王炎言：「臨安居民繁夥，河港堙塞，雖屢開導，緣裁減工費，不能迄功。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Qiandao, the Jingnan prefect Wang Yan said: "Lin'an's residents are numerous; river channels are blocked; though dredged repeatedly, reduced funds prevent finishing."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Qiandao, Prefect of Jingnan Wang Yan wrote: "Lin'an is densely populated and its channels silted; despite repeated dredging, cuts to the budget keep the work from completion."

sentences.zh: 臣嘗措置開河錢十萬緡，乞候農暇，特詔有司，用此專充開河支費，庶幾河渠復通，公私為利。

translations.literal: I once set aside a hundred thousand strings for dredging; I beg that after the farming slack a special edict direct officials to use this solely for dredging expenses, so channels may reopen to public and private benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I have set aside a hundred thousand strings for dredging; I ask that after the harvest slack the court direct officials to use it solely for that purpose, so the channels may reopen for public and private good.

sentences.zh: 」上俞其請。

translations.literal: The throne assented to his request.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，守臣周淙出公帑錢招集遊民，開浚城內外河，疏通淤塞，人以治辦稱之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Prefect Zhou Cong spent public funds to recruit vagrants, dredging rivers inside and outside the city, clearing blockage — people praised his governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Prefect Zhou Cong spent public funds to hire vagrants to dredge the inner and outer waterways and clear blockages; he won praise for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，兩浙漕臣趙磻老言：「臨安府長安閘至許村巡檢司一帶，漕河淺澀，請出錢米，發兩岸人戶出力開浚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi, the Zhejiang transport commissioner Zhao Panlao said: "From Lin'an's Chang'an Sluice to Xucun Inspectorate the transport canal is shallow; I ask to supply cash and grain and mobilize households on both banks."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunxi, Transport Commissioner Zhao Panlao of the two Zhe circuits wrote: "From Chang'an Sluice to Xucun Inspectorate the transport canal is shoaling; I ask for funds and grain to mobilize households on both banks to dredge."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「欲于通江橋置板閘，遇城中河水淺涸，啟板納潮，繼即下板，固護水勢，不得通舟；

translations.literal: He also said: "I wish to set a plank sluice at Tongjiang Bridge; when city water is shallow, open the planks to admit tide, then lower them to hold the water level and bar vessels;"
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed a plank sluice at Tongjiang Bridge: when city water runs low, open the planks to admit tide, then close them to hold the level — though boats could not pass while they were shut;

sentences.zh: 若河水不乏，即收閘板，聽舟楫往還為便。」

translations.literal: If river water is ample, collect the planks and allow boats to pass freely."
translations.idiomatic: when water is ample, remove the planks and let shipping pass as usual."

sentences.zh: 七年，守臣吳淵言：「萬松嶺兩旁古渠，多被權勢及有司公吏之家造屋侵佔，及內砦前石橋、都亭驛橋南北河道，居民多拋糞土瓦礫，以致填塞，流水不通。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Prefect Wu Yuan said: "Ancient channels beside Wansong Ridge are encroached by the powerful and clerks' households; before Inner Fortress stone bridge and north and south of Duting Post Bridge residents dump filth and rubble, blocking flow."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Prefect Wu Yuan reported: "Ancient channels beside Wansong Ridge have been built over by the powerful and by officials' families; north and south of the Inner Fortress stone bridge and Duting Post Bridge residents dump refuse and rubble until the water cannot flow."

sentences.zh: 今欲分委兩通判監督，地分廂巡，逐時點檢，勿令侵佔並拋颺糞土。

translations.literal: Now I wish to assign two vice-prefects to supervise, district patrols to inspect constantly, forbidding encroachment and dumping.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to assign two vice-prefects to supervise, with ward patrols to inspect constantly and forbid encroachment and dumping.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，若不淤塞，各減一年磨勘；

translations.literal: At term's end, if no silting, reduce each's merit review by one year;
translations.idiomatic: At the end of their terms, if no silting occurs, each official gets one year shaved from his merit review;

sentences.zh: 違，展一年，以示勸懲。」

translations.literal: If violated, add one year, to show encouragement and punishment."
translations.idiomatic: if not, add one year — as reward and warning."

sentences.zh: 十四年七月，不雨，臣僚言：「竊見奉口至北新橋三十六里，斷港絕潢，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, without rain, an official said: "I observe from Fengkou to North New Bridge thirty-six li — broken channels, none worse."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, during drought, an official wrote: "From Fengkou to North New Bridge, thirty-six li of channel are cut off — nowhere is worse."

sentences.zh: 今宜開浚，使通客船，以平谷直。

translations.literal: Now it should be dredged so passenger boats pass and valley prices level.
translations.idiomatic: It should be dredged now so passenger boats can pass and grain prices may ease.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 鹽官海水

translations.literal: Seawater at Yanguan
translations.idiomatic: Seawater at Yanguan

sentences.zh: 鹽官海水：嘉定十二年，臣僚言：「鹽官去海三十餘里，舊無海患，縣以鹽灶頗盛，課利易登。

translations.literal: Seawater at Yanguan: In the twelfth year of Jiading, an official said: "Yanguan is thirty-odd li from the sea; formerly no sea calamity; the county's salt works flourish and levies easy to collect."
translations.idiomatic: Seawater at Yanguan: In the twelfth year of Jiading, an official wrote: "Yanguan lies thirty-odd li from the sea and once knew no tidal harm; its salt works are prosperous and levies easy to raise."

sentences.zh: 去歲海水泛漲，湍激橫沖，沙岸每一潰裂，嘗數十丈。

translations.literal: Last year the sea surged; torrents struck crosswise; each breach of the sand shore was often tens of zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the sea rose; surging currents smashed the sand banks, each breach tens of zhang wide.

sentences.zh: 日復一日，浸入鹵地，蘆州港瀆，蕩為一壑。

translations.literal: Day after day it encroached on brine fields; Luzhou harbor channels were scoured into one ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day it ate into the brine flats; Luzhou harbor was scoured into a single gulf.

sentences.zh: 今聞潮勢深入，逼近居民。

translations.literal: Now we hear the tide presses inland, nearing residents.
translations.idiomatic: We now hear the tide pushing inland toward settled neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 萬一春水驟漲，怒濤奔湧，海風佐之，則呼吸蕩出，百里之民，寧不俱葬魚腹乎？

translations.literal: Should spring waters suddenly rise, furious waves rush, sea winds aid them — in a breath they may scour out; will not the people for a hundred li all be buried in fish bellies?
translations.idiomatic: Should spring floods and angry seas rise together with a sea wind, in an instant a hundred li of people could be swept to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 況京畿赤縣，密邇都城。

translations.literal: Moreover this is a metropolitan red county, close to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this is a metropolitan county hard by the capital.

sentences.zh: 內有二十五里塘，直通長安閘，上徹臨平，下接崇德，漕運往來，客船絡繹，兩岸田畝，無非沃壤。

translations.literal: Within is the twenty-five-li embankment, running straight to Chang'an Sluice, reaching Linping above and Chongde below; transport and passenger boats thread together; both banks' fields are rich soil.
translations.idiomatic: Within lies the twenty-five-li embankment road to Chang'an Sluice, reaching Linping upstream and Chongde downstream — transport and passenger craft in constant passage, and fertile fields on both banks.

sentences.zh: 若海水徑入於塘，不惟民田有咸水渰沒之患，而裏河堤岸，亦將有潰裂之憂。

translations.literal: If seawater enters the embankment directly, not only will people's fields suffer salt drowning but inner river banks may burst.
translations.idiomatic: If the sea breaks through the embankment, not only will fields be drowned in brine but the inner river banks may collapse as well.

sentences.zh: 乞下浙西諸司，條具築捺之策，務使捍堤堅壯，土脈充實，不為怒潮所沖。

translations.literal: I beg orders to western Zhe offices to itemize dike-building plans, making seawalls firm and soil solid, not to be struck by angry tides.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that western Zhe authorities draw up dike plans so the seawall stands firm and packed, not to be torn by raging tide.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 十五年，都省言：鹽官縣海塘沖決，命浙西提舉劉垕專任其事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the Secretariat said: Yanguan County seawall breached; ordered Western Zhe intendant Liu Huang to take sole charge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Secretariat reported that Yanguan County's seawall had breached and assigned Western Zhe Intendant Liu Huang to take charge.

sentences.zh: 既而垕言：

translations.literal: Then Huang said:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huang then reported:

sentences.zh: 縣東接海鹽，西距仁和，北抵崇德、德清，境連平江、嘉興、湖州；

translations.literal: East the county borders Haiyan; west it faces Renhe; north Chongde and Deqing; borders Pingjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou;
translations.idiomatic: East it borders Haiyan, west Renhe, north Chongde and Deqing, and its jurisdiction touches Pingjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou;

sentences.zh: 南瀕大海元與縣治相去四十餘里。

translations.literal: South it faced the great sea; formerly the seat was forty-odd li from the sea.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay the open sea, once forty-odd li from the county seat.

sentences.zh: 數年以來，水失故道，早晚兩潮，奔沖向北，遂致縣南四十餘里盡淪為海。

translations.literal: In recent years water lost its old course; morning and evening tides rushed north; thus forty-odd li south of the seat were all lost to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the water lost its old course; morning and evening tides drove north, and forty-odd li south of the seat have been lost to the sea.

sentences.zh: 近縣之南，元有捍海古塘亙二十里。

translations.literal: Near the county's south had been an ancient seawall twenty li long.
translations.idiomatic: South of the county once ran an ancient seawall twenty li long.

sentences.zh: 今東西兩段，並已淪毀，侵入縣兩旁又各三四里，止存中間古塘十餘里。

translations.literal: Now both eastern and western sections are ruined; the sea has encroached three or four li on either side of the seat; only the middle ancient wall of ten-odd li remains.
translations.idiomatic: Both eastern and western sections are gone; the sea has eaten three or four li on either flank of the seat, leaving only ten-odd li of the old wall in the middle.

sentences.zh: 萬一水勢沖激不已，不惟鹽官一縣不可復存，而向北地勢卑下，所慮咸流入蘇、秀、湖三州等處，則田畝不可種植，大為利害。

translations.literal: Should the water strike without cease, not only Yanguan county may not survive; north the land is low — we fear brine flowing into Suzhou, Xiu, and Hu circuits — then fields cannot be planted; great harm.
translations.idiomatic: If the tide keeps breaking through, Yanguan may not survive; and to the north the land lies low — brine could reach Suzhou, Xiu, and Hu, ruining farmland across a vast region.

sentences.zh: 詳今日之患，大概有二：一曰陸地淪毀，二曰鹹潮泛溢。

translations.literal: Today's woes fall into two: first, land lost to destruction; second, salt tide overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Today's troubles fall under two heads: land swallowed by the sea, and salt tide spreading inland.

sentences.zh: 陸地淪毀者，固無力可施；

translations.literal: For lost land nothing can be done;
translations.idiomatic: For land already lost, nothing can be done;

sentences.zh: 鹹潮泛溢者，乃因捍海古塘沖損，遇大潮必盤越流注北向，宜築土塘以捍鹹潮。

translations.literal: For salt tide overflow, because the ancient seawall is broken, great tides spill north — an earthen wall should be built against brine.
translations.idiomatic: For spreading brine, the old seawall is breached and great tides pour north — we should build earthen dikes against the salt tide.

sentences.zh: 所築塘基址，南北各有兩處：在縣東近南則為六十里鹹塘，近北則為袁花塘；

translations.literal: Sites for building, north and south each have two: east of the seat, near south is the Sixty-Li Salt Dike, near north Yuanhua Dike;
translations.idiomatic: Dike sites fall in two pairs north and south of the seat: to the east, the Sixty-Li Salt Dike in the south and Yuanhua Dike in the north;

sentences.zh: 在縣西近南亦曰鹹塘，近北則為淡塘。

translations.literal: West of the seat near south also Salt Dike, near north Fresh Dike.
translations.idiomatic: to the west, the Salt Dike in the south and Fresh Dike in the north.

sentences.zh: 亦嘗驗兩處土色虛實，則袁花塘、淡塘差勝鹹塘，且各近裏，未至與海潮為敵。

translations.literal: Soil was tested at both places: Yuanhua and Fresh dikes are somewhat better than Salt Dike, and each lies nearer inland, not yet meeting the sea tide as foe.
translations.idiomatic: Testing the soil at each site, Yuanhua and Fresh dikes are sounder than the Salt Dike and lie farther inland, not yet exposed head-on to the open tide.

sentences.zh: 勢當東就袁花塘、西就淡塘修築，則可以禦縣東鹹潮盤溢之患。

translations.literal: The plan should build east on Yuanhua Dike and west on Fresh Dike to ward off eastern salt-tide overflow.
translations.idiomatic: We should build on Yuanhua to the east and Fresh Dike to the west to hold back the salt tide spilling from the east.

sentences.zh: 其縣西一帶淡塘，連縣治左右，共五十餘里，合先修築。

translations.literal: The western Fresh Dike belt along the seat, fifty-odd li total, should be built first.
translations.idiomatic: The western Fresh Dike belt along the seat, more than fifty li in all, should be built first.

sentences.zh: 兼縣南去海一里余，幸而古塘尚存，縣治民居，盡在其中，未可棄之度外。

translations.literal: Moreover south of the seat is but a li from the sea; happily the ancient wall remains; seat and homes lie within — not to be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The seat lies little more than a li from the sea; fortunately the old wall still stands and shelters the seat and its people — we must not abandon it.

sentences.zh: 今將見管樁石，就古塘稍加工築疊一里許，為防護縣治之計。

translations.literal: Now available piles and stone will reinforce the ancient wall for about a li to protect the seat.
translations.idiomatic: We will use available piles and stone to raise the old wall about a li as a shield for the seat.

sentences.zh: 其縣東民戶，日築六十里鹹塘。

translations.literal: Eastern households daily build the Sixty-Li Salt Dike.
translations.idiomatic: Households to the east are raising the Sixty-Li Salt Dike day by day.

sentences.zh: 萬一又為海潮沖損，當計用樁木修築袁花塘以捍之。

translations.literal: Should it again be struck by tide, plan to use piles to build Yuanhua Dike against it.
translations.idiomatic: If the tide breaks through again, we should build Yuanhua Dike with piles as a second line of defense.

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The throne agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 明州水

translations.literal: Waters of Ming Prefecture
translations.idiomatic: Waters of Ming Prefecture

sentences.zh: 明州水：紹興五年，明州守臣李光奏：「明、越陂湖，專溉農田。

translations.literal: Waters of Ming Prefecture: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Ming Prefect Li Guang memorialized: "Ming and Yue reservoir lakes solely irrigate farmland."
translations.idiomatic: Waters of Ming Prefecture: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Prefect Li Guang of Ming wrote: "The reservoir lakes of Ming and Yue exist solely to irrigate farmland."

sentences.zh: 自慶曆中，始有盜湖為田者，三司使切責漕臣，嚴立法禁。

translations.literal: From Qingli onward some stole lakes for fields; the Fiscal Commissioner sharply rebuked transport officials and set strict laws.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qingli era some began reclaiming lakes as farmland; the fiscal commissioner sharply rebuked transport officials and imposed strict prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 宣和以來，王仲薿守越，樓異守明，創為應奉，始廢湖為田，自是歲有水旱之患。

translations.literal: Since Xuanhe, Wang Zhongmou governed Yue and Lou Yi Ming, creating tribute projects, first abolishing lakes for fields — hence yearly flood and drought woes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xuanhe, when Wang Zhongmou governed Yue and Lou Yi governed Ming, they launched tribute projects, first draining the lakes for fields — and flood and drought have followed every year since.

sentences.zh: 乞行廢罷，盡復為湖。

translations.literal: I beg to abolish these and wholly restore the lakes.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these projects be abolished and the lakes fully restored.

sentences.zh: 如江東、西之圩田，蘇、秀之圍田，皆當講究興復。

translations.literal: Like Jiangdong and Jiangxi polder fields, Suzhou and Xiu encircled fields — all should be studied for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The polders of Jiangdong and Jiangxi and the encircled fields of Suzhou and Xiu should likewise be examined for restoration.

sentences.zh: 」詔逐路轉運司相度聞奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered each circuit transport office to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Edict to each circuit transport commission to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，守臣張津言：「東錢湖容受七十二溪，方圓廣闊八百頃，傍山為固，疊石為塘八十里。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao, Prefect Zhang Jin said: "East Qian Lake receives seventy-two streams, eight hundred qing in area, mountains as flank, stone piled for eighty li of embankment."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiandao, Prefect Zhang Jin wrote: "East Qian Lake catches seventy-two streams, covers eight hundred qing, is braced by mountains, and is ringed by eighty li of stone embankment."

sentences.zh: 自唐天寶三年，縣令陸南金開廣之。

translations.literal: Since Tang Tianbao year 3, Magistrate Lu Nanjin enlarged it.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Lu Nanjin enlarged it in the third year of Tang Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 國朝天禧元年，郡守李夷庚重修之。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's Tianxi year 1, the prefect Li Yigeng rebuilt it.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Yigeng rebuilt it in the first year of our Tianxi reign.

sentences.zh: 中有四閘七堰，凡遇旱涸，開閘放水，溉田五十萬畝。

translations.literal: Within are four sluices and seven weirs; in drought they open to irrigate five hundred thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: It has four sluices and seven weirs; in drought they are opened to water five hundred thousand mu of fields.

sentences.zh: 比因豪民於湖塘淺岸漸次包占，種植菱荷，障塞湖水。

translations.literal: Lately powerful families have encroached on shallow shores, planting water chestnuts and lotus, blocking lake water.
translations.idiomatic: Lately powerful families have encroached on the shallows, planting water chestnuts and lotus and choking the lake.

sentences.zh: 紹興十八年，雖曾檢舉約束，盡罷請佃。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Shaoxing investigation restrained them and ended all petitions for lease.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Shaoxing, though investigators forbade this and ended all lease petitions,

translations.literal: Years on, chestnut roots spread, seeping and blocking water channels, harming storage;
translations.idiomatic: over the years water-chestnut roots have spread, seeping into channels and impeding storage;

sentences.zh: 兼塘岸間有低塌處，若不淘浚修築，不惟浸失水利，兼恐塘埂相繼摧毀。

translations.literal: Moreover the embankment has low collapsed spots; without dredging and repair, not only is water benefit lost but the dike may fall in succession.
translations.idiomatic: and stretches of embankment have sagged. Without dredging and repair we will lose its benefit and risk the dike collapsing in succession.

sentences.zh: 乞候農隙趁時開鑿，因得土修治埂岸，實為兩便。

translations.literal: I beg to wait for farming slack and dredge timely, gaining soil to repair banks — truly two benefits.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to dredge in the farming slack, using the spoil to repair the banks — a double gain.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 鄞縣水

translations.literal: Waters of Yin County
translations.idiomatic: Waters of Yin County

sentences.zh: 鄞縣水：嘉定十四年，慶元府言：「鄞縣水自四明諸山溪澗會至他山，置堰小涇，下江入河。

translations.literal: Waters of Yin County: In the fourteenth year of Jiading, Qingyuan prefecture said: "Yin County water gathers from Siming streams to Tashan, sets weirs at Xiaojing, enters the river."
translations.idiomatic: Waters of Yin County: In the fourteenth year of Jiading, Qingyuan prefecture reported: "Yin County's water gathers from Siming's mountain streams at Tashan, where weirs at Xiaojing send it down to the main river."

sentences.zh: 所入上河之水，專溉民田，其利甚博。

translations.literal: Water entering the upper river solely irrigates fields — the benefit is very broad.
translations.idiomatic: The water entering the upper river irrigates farmland alone — the benefit is vast.

sentences.zh: 比因淤塞，堰上山觜少有溪水流入上河。

translations.literal: Lately silting leaves but little stream entering the upper river from the weir mountain spur.
translations.idiomatic: Lately silt has left only a trickle from the weir spur into the upper river.

sentences.zh: 自春徂夏不雨，令官吏發卒開淘沙觜及浚港汊，又於堰上壘疊沙石，逼使溪流兗入上河。

translations.literal: From spring to summer without rain, officials sent troops to dredge the sand spur and channels; piled sand and stone on the weir to force the stream west into the upper river.
translations.idiomatic: With no rain from spring through summer, officials sent laborers to dredge the sand spur and channels and piled stone on the weir to force the stream into the upper river.

sentences.zh: 其他山水入府城南門一帶，有碶閘三所：曰烏金，曰積瀆，曰行春。

translations.literal: Other mountain water entering south of the prefectural city has three sluices: Wujin, Jidu, and Xingchun.
translations.idiomatic: Other mountain streams entering south of the city pass three sluice-gates: Wujin, Jidu, and Xingchun.

sentences.zh: 烏金碶又名上水碶，昔因倒損，遂捺為壩，以致淤沙在河，或遇溪流聚湧，時復沖倒所捺壩，走泄水源。

translations.literal: Wujin Sluice, also Upper-Water Sluice, once collapsed and was dammed, silt filled the river; when streams surged the dam was sometimes washed out, leaking the source.
translations.idiomatic: Wujin Sluice, also called Upper-Water Sluice, once collapsed and was dammed off, letting silt fill the channel; when surges came they sometimes washed out the dam and drained the upland supply.

sentences.zh: 行春橋又名南石碶，碶面石板之下，歲久損壞空虛，每受潮水，演溢奔突，山于石縫，以致鹹潮盡入上河。

translations.literal: Xingchun Bridge, also South Stone Sluice — beneath its stone slabs, years of damage left voids; each tide surged through stone seams, so brine entirely entered the upper river.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchun Bridge, also South Stone Sluice, has voids under its slabs from age; each tide surges through the seams and brine floods the upper river.

sentences.zh: 其縣東管有道士堰，至白鶴橋一帶，河港堙塞；

translations.literal: East of the county is Daoshi Weir to Baihe Bridge — channels blocked;
translations.idiomatic: East of the county, from Daoshi Weir to Baihe Bridge, the channels are blocked;

sentences.zh: 又有朱賴堰，與行春等碶相連，堰下江流通徹大海。

translations.literal: Also Zhulai Weir, connected to Xingchun and other sluices — below the weir the river reaches the sea.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhulai Weir, linked to Xingchun and the other sluices, whose lower reach opens to the sea.

sentences.zh: 今春闕雨，上河乾淺，堰身塌損，以致鹹潮透入上河，使農民不敢車注溉田。

translations.literal: This spring lacked rain; upper river ran dry and shallow; weir body collapsed — brine seeped in and farmers dared not scoop water for fields.
translations.idiomatic: This spring's drought left the upper river shallow and the weirs damaged, letting brine through so farmers dare not lift water for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 乞修砌上水、烏金諸處壩堰，仍選清強能幹職官，專一提督。」

translations.literal: I beg repair of Upper-Water, Wujin, and other dams; select capable officials to supervise exclusively."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Upper-Water, Wujin, and the other dams be rebuilt, and that able officials be chosen to supervise the work."

sentences.zh: 潤州水

translations.literal: Waters of Run Prefecture
translations.idiomatic: Waters of Run Prefecture

sentences.zh: 潤州水：紹興七年，兩浙轉運使向子諲言：「鎮江府呂城、夾岡，形勢高仰，因春夏不雨，官漕艱勤。

translations.literal: Waters of Run Prefecture: In the seventh year of Shaoxing, the two-Zhe transport commissioner Xiang Ziyin said: "Zhenjiang's Lücheng and Jiagang lie high; because spring and summer lacked rain, official transport was arduous."
translations.idiomatic: Waters of Run Prefecture: In the seventh year of Shaoxing, Transport Commissioner Xiang Ziyin of the two Zhe circuits wrote: "At Zhenjiang, Lücheng and Jiagang stand high; with no spring or summer rain, official grain transport has grown arduous."

sentences.zh: 尋遣官屬李澗詢究練湖本末，始知此湖在唐永泰間已廢而復興。

translations.literal: Soon he sent the official Li Jian to investigate Lian Lake's history — learning it was abolished and revived in Tang Yongtai.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his subordinate Li Jian to trace Lian Lake's history and learned that it had been abandoned and revived in the Tang Yongtai era.

sentences.zh: 今堤岸弛禁，致有侵佃冒決，故湖水不能瀦蓄，舟楫不通，公私告病。

translations.literal: Now dikes are lax and encroachment and illegal breaches occur — lake water cannot be stored, boats cannot pass, public and private complain of affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Now the dikes are poorly guarded, encroachment and illegal breaches abound, the lake cannot hold water, boats cannot pass, and public and private interests alike suffer.

sentences.zh: 若夏秋霖潦，則丹陽、金壇、延陵一帶良田，亦被渰沒。

translations.literal: If summer-autumn heavy rain and flood, then Danyang, Jintan, Yanling belt good fields, also are inundated.
translations.idiomatic: When summer and autumn bring heavy rains and floods, the fine farmland around Danyang, Jintan, and Yanling is submerged as well.

sentences.zh: 臣已令丹陽知縣朱穆等增置二斗門、一石鹈達，及修補堤防，盡復舊跡，庶為永久之利。

translations.literal: Your servant has ordered Danyang magistrate Zhu Mu and others to add two sluice gates and one stone dam, and repair dikes, fully restoring old traces, that there may be lasting benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered Magistrate Zhu Mu of Danyang and others to add two sluice gates and a stone dam, repair the dikes, and fully restore the old works, for lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 」乾道七年，以臣僚言：「丹陽練湖幅員四十里，納長山諸水，漕渠資之，故古語云：'湖水寸，渠水尺。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year of Qiandao, on officials' words: "Danyang Lian Lake spans forty li, receives Changshan and other waters, the transport canal relies on it — hence the old saying: 'An inch of lake water, a foot of canal water.'
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qiandao, on memorial from the officials: "Danyang's Lian Lake spans forty li, taking in the waters of Changshan and elsewhere; the grain transport canal depends on it — hence the old saying: 'An inch on the lake, a foot in the canal.'

sentences.zh: 」在唐之禁甚嚴，盜決者罪比殺人。

translations.literal: " In Tang the prohibition was very strict; illegal breachers were punished like murderers.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times the prohibition was severe: those who breached the lake illegally were punished like murderers.

sentences.zh: 本朝浸緩其禁以惠民，然修築嚴甚。

translations.literal: Our dynasty has gradually eased the prohibition to benefit the people, yet maintenance remains strict.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has gradually relaxed the prohibition to benefit the people, yet upkeep of the works remains strict.

sentences.zh: 春夏多雨之際，瀦蓄盈滿，雖秋無雨，漕渠或淺，但泄湖水一寸，則為河一尺矣。

translations.literal: In spring-summer rainy season, impoundment fills; though autumn has no rain, if the transport canal is shallow, releasing one inch of lake water raises the river one foot.
translations.idiomatic: In the rainy spring and summer the reservoir fills; even if autumn is dry and the canal runs shallow, releasing one inch of lake water raises the river a foot.

sentences.zh: 兵變以後，多廢不治，堤岸圮闕，不能貯水；

translations.literal: After the military upheaval, much was abandoned and untended; dikes collapsed and could not store water;
translations.idiomatic: After the military upheavals much was abandoned; the dikes crumbled and could no longer hold water;

sentences.zh: 強家因而專利，耕以為田，遂致淤澱。

translations.literal: Powerful families then monopolized profit, farming it as fields, and silt accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: powerful families then seized the profit, farming the lakebed as fields, until silt choked it.

sentences.zh: 歲月既久，其害滋廣。

translations.literal: As years passed, the harm grew wider.
translations.idiomatic: As the years passed, the damage spread.

sentences.zh: 望責長吏浚治堙塞，立為盜決侵耕之法，著於令。

translations.literal: We hope senior officials will be charged to dredge blockages, establish laws against illegal breach and encroachment farming, and record them in statutes.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that senior officials be made responsible for dredging blockages, that laws against illegal breach and encroachment be enacted, and that they be written into the code.

sentences.zh: 庶幾練湖漸復其舊，民田獲灌溉之利，漕渠無淺涸之患。

translations.literal: Thus Lian Lake may gradually return to its former state, people's fields gain irrigation benefit, and the transport canal suffers no shallow-dry affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Then Lian Lake may gradually return to its former state, the people's fields will gain irrigation, and the transport canal will be spared shallow water and drought.

sentences.zh: 」詔兩浙漕臣沈度專一措置修築。

translations.literal: " Edict ordering the two-Zhe transport official Shen Du exclusively to arrange repair and construction.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Transport Commissioner Shen Du of the two Zhe circuits to take sole charge of repairs.

sentences.zh: 慶元五年，兩浙轉運、浙西提舉言：「以鎮江府守臣重修呂城兩閘畢，再造一新閘以固堤防，庶為便利。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingyuan, the two-Zhe transport commission and western Zhejiang intendant reported: "With the Zhenjiang prefect having finished rebuilding the two gates at Lücheng, build one new gate further to strengthen the dikes, for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qingyuan, the two-Zhe transport commission and the western Zhejiang intendant reported: "Now that the Zhenjiang prefect has finished rebuilding the two sluices at Lücheng, a new sluice should be built to strengthen the dikes, for the general good."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 浙西運河，自臨安府北郭務至鎮江江口閘，六百四十一里。

translations.literal: The western Zhejiang transport canal, from Lin'an North Guo Wu to Zhenjiang river-mouth sluice, is six hundred forty-one li.
translations.idiomatic: The western Zhejiang transport canal runs six hundred forty-one li from Lin'an's North Guo Station to the river-mouth sluice at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 淳熙七年，帝因輔臣奏金使往來事，曰：「運河有淺狹處，可令守臣以漸開浚，庶不擾民。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chunxi, the emperor, when aides reported on Jin envoys' travel, said: "Where the canal is shallow and narrow, local officials may dredge gradually, so the people are not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chunxi, when his aides reported on the passage of Jin envoys, the emperor said: "Where the canal is shallow and narrow, let local officials dredge it step by step, so the people are not disturbed."

sentences.zh: 」至十一年冬，臣僚言：「運河之浚，自北關至秀州杉青，各有堰閘，自可瀦水。

translations.literal: " By winter of the eleventh year, officials reported: "Canal dredging from North Gate to Xiuzhou Shanqing — each stretch has weirs and sluices that can store water.
translations.idiomatic: By the winter of the eleventh year, officials reported: "From North Gate to Xiuzhou's Shanqing, the canal has weirs and sluices at each stage that can hold water.

sentences.zh: 惟沿河上塘有小堰數處，積久低陷，無以防遏水勢，當以時加修治。

translations.literal: Only along the upper embankment are several small weirs long sunk low, unable to check the water's force — they should be repaired in season.
translations.idiomatic: Only along the upper embankment are several small weirs that have long since sagged and can no longer check the current; these should be repaired in season."
